comments.body:
Deploy preview for *algolia-instantsearch* ready!

Built with commit 02600ee153ee3aff19cd1c93222ed6d04769b048

https://deploy-preview-3245--algolia-instantsearch.netlify.com

It seems to work now, indeed.

The thing is that these are generated with [Doctoc](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/develop/package.json#L22), which will override your changes every time the command is run again.

The easy solution that I see right now would be to either find emojis that work in links, or remove all emojis in headers.

@francoischalifour open issue re: emojis in headers - https://github.com/thlorenz/anchor-markdown-header/issues/36

Seems that the regex doesn't capture all emojis properly thus some work and some don't. I think the cleanest solution is to remove them entirely.

Thanks for pointing to this issue (I noticed the faulty behavior but didn't expect it to be an actual issue in the Markdown parser).

I'm for removing the emojis in headers if @algolia/instantsearch-for-websites agrees.

Let's just remove those emoji then, when I checked earlier the old links were working, and the new ones were, but that seemed to depend from which place on GitHub I was viewing it (the diff view did work and the main one doesn't lol). 

Let's remove the confusion, and get rid of the 2+ byte emoji
PR updated with emojis removed and ToC re-generated via `doctoc`
